nodes.text: Watch the hens. They've decided feet are a delicacy. What do you need?

choices.text: Spare an egg for the road?
How do you plan a farm year?

nodes.text: Next spring, the south strip goes to cotton. Jorel says the soil's wrong. The soil and I had a word in private, and the soil is *enthusiastic*. Tilo's loom sits hungry half the year, and every bolt of cloth in this town came in on a cart. We could grow it and spin it and weave it inside our own fence. Watch me.
Here. Laid this morning, and the hen wants you to know it was her best work. {item:egg} Crack it over a pan at any campfire.

In the seed ledger, in winter, by lamplight: every row, every rotation, three seasons deep. Jorel digs what I draw and swears the drawing's the easy half. He's right, too. The ledger doesn't get blisters.
Mind the gate latch. The cows have learnt Perl's, and mine's likely next.
